decisions.reason: As a flagship reusable harvesting crate aligned with the firm's sustainability-led packaging strategy, it is likely to stay unless demand proved far below plan.
A foldable large-container line with several models fits the firm's core reusable logistics offering and likely justifies ongoing support in a large industrial portfolio.
A stackable plastic crate is a standard, strategically compatible transport-packaging product, so a large manufacturer would usually retain it unless margins were clearly weak.
A medium-duty rackable pallet remains close to the firm's established pallet business, though some risk exists from overlap with other pallet formats and portfolio rationalization.
The spill-retention pallet serves a narrower compliance-driven niche, so it faces higher pruning risk, but it still broadens the firm's pallet range and can support specialized customers.
A single plastic pallet variant with load retainers appears more vulnerable to consolidation because its function can often be covered by customized or broader pallet lines already in the portfolio.
